end.summary:
Harsh practised reading and plotting ordered pairs on a coordinate grid.
They identified left/right and up/down moves and named quadrants, including Quadrant II.
They practised plotting (-1, -2) and (1, 4) from the origin.
They initially treated (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same point; this was corrected in turn 12, but the misconception had appeared earlier as well.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Harsh practised using the ordered-pair rule: move along x first, then y, and identify the resulting quadrant. They explained that negative one means left and four means up, and later corrected the mix-up that (3, 2) and (2, 3) are different points because the moves happen in a different order. At home, ask them to plot a few pairs in both orders, such as (2, 3) and (3, 2), and label each point.
